article.locator: §2.1–2.2; Figures 1–3; Data Availability. Jesús de la Morena, Francisco Ramos, Andrés Vázquez. The article identifies vision-marker circle fitting as the curvature source and electrical input to the regulator as the system input.

evidence: Public data underlying a laboratory experiment; the CSV has exactly three fields Input, Output and Time, with no units in the header. It does not include the raw camera stream or the regulator’s separately described pressure reading.
coverage: 240001 finite strictly increasing time rows, four consecutive triangular cycles sharing boundary minima; 60000 increments per cycle and 30000 per half-cycle. Use file command 0..1 and output as published, without rescaling or assigning physical units.
comparison: Article states 0.05 Hz, 2 V, four cycles, and normalization of both quantities for the hysteresis figure. In the archive the four cycles peak at source Time = 1000, 3000, 5000 and 7000 (source period 2000), Input peaks at 1, and Output ranges from 0.0012206050 to 0.0168373877. Unknown export time scaling prevents estimating physical rate/lag from the Time header. The file is an input–output series; no pre-limit/post-limit command pair or sensor of mechanical load is present.
method: Identify the five exact minima and four maxima of Input. For each strictly monotone pair of branches interpolate Output at the same Input 0.25, 0.50 and 0.75. Integrate each branch over increasing Input by trapezoids; subtract rising branch area from falling branch area. Full cycles are not independent actuators or cross-session trials. Endpoint curvature is allowed to drift.
